title: Ex 2.6 #13 · P ∨ (Q ∧ R) vs (P ∨ Q) ∧ R
prompt: Are $P \vee (Q \wedge R)$ and $(P \vee Q) \wedge R$ logically equivalent? Decide, and back up your answer with a truth table, a chain of known equivalences, or a row where the two statements differ.
answer_format: equivalent or not equivalent. Steps are optional: truth-table columns, rewrite steps, or a row like P = T, Q = F where the two statements differ.
hints: Moving the parentheses changes which connective is applied last.
Try a row where P is true and R is false.
solution: Take $P$ true and $Q$, $R$ false. Then $P \vee (Q \wedge R)$ is true, because $P$ is.
But $(P \vee Q) \wedge R$ is false, because $R$ is.
So the statements are not logically equivalent.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses logical equivalence (Section 2.6).
